DEFINITIONS AND BASIC PROVISIONS

This Retail Lease Agreement is a part of the document designated Basic Lease Terms (The “BASIC LEASE TERMS”),
which was contemporaneously executed by Landlord and Tenant. If any conflict exists between the Basic Lease Terms and this
Retail Lease Agreement, then this Retail Lease Agreement shall control. The definitions and basic provisions set forth in the
Basic Lease Terms are incorporated in this Retail Lease Agreement by reference for all purposes. This retail Lease Agreement
and the Basic Lease Terms are together referred to as the “LEASE”.
The following terms shall have the meanings set forth:
1.1
“ADA”: The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, and all rules, regulations and guidelines promulgated
thereunder, as the same may be amended from time to time.
1.2
“BUILDING STANDARD”: The type, brand, quality and quantity of materials Landlord designates from
time to time to be the minimum quality and quantity to be used in the Shopping Center, or the exclusive type, grade, quality and
quantity of materials to be used in the Shopping Center.
1.3
“COMMON AREAS”: Those parts of the Shopping center which are designated by Landlord from time to
time for the common use or benefit of tenants generally or the public, including without limitation, parking area, private streets
and alleys, landscaping, curbs, loading areas, sidewalks, malls, promenades (enclosed or otherwise), lighting facilities, drinking
fountains, meeting rooms, public toilets, those areas devoted to corridors, mechanical rooms, janitorial closets, electrical and
telephone closets and vending areas, (but not any such areas within another tenant’s premises). The term “Common Areas” shall
not include ( a ) streets and alleys maintained by a public authority, ( b ) areas within the Shopping Center which may from time
to time not be owned by Landlord (unless subject to a cross-access agreement benefiting an area which includes the Premises)
and ( c ) areas leased to a single purpose, free-standing user where access is restricted (such as a bank or fast-food restaurant). In
addition, although the roof(s) of the building(s) in the Shopping Center are not literally part of the Common Area, they will be
deemed to be so included for purposes of ( d ) Landlord’s ability to prescribe rules and regulations regarding same and ( e ) their
inclusion for purposes of Operating Expenses under Article 5. Landlord reserves the right to add to or delete from, or change,
from time to time, the dimensions and locations of any part of the Common Area, as well as the dimensions, identity and type of
any buildings in the Shopping Center.
1.4
“CONTRACT RATE” The per annum rate equal to the lesser of ( a ) five percent (5%) plus the federal
discount rate at the time of this lease or ( b ) the highest lawful rate. The highest lawful rate is the greatest of the rates of interest
from time to time permitted under applicable federal and state law.
1.5
“HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES”: Any substances declared to be hazardous or toxic under any law or
regulation now or hereafter enacted or promulgated by any governmental authority having jurisdiction.
1.6

“LANDLORD’S MORTGAGEE”: Landlord’s Mortgagee is defined in Subparagraph 14.1.

1.7
“MANAGER”: One or more entities or persons designated by Landlord from time to time, in Landlord’s sole
discretion, to manage all or part of the Shopping center. The current Manager is designated in the Basic Lease Terms. Landlord
may change Manager at any time without notice to or consent from Tenant.
1.8
“PUNCH LIST ITEMS”: Any details of Premises construction, mechanical adjustment or similar matters
deemed incomplete in the reasonable judgment of Landlord’s architect, the noncompletion of which do not materially interfere
with Tenant’s use of Premises. If Landlord is not using an architect, then Landlord shall make the judgments concerning the
Punch List Items, so long as Landlord’s judgments are reasonable.
1.9
“RENTABLE AREA”: The number of square feet of floor area in the Premises or in enclosed buildings
which are erected on portions of the Shopping Center and which are designed for tenant use and occupancy. All such floor area
shall be fixed as of the last day of the applicable time period and shall be measured from the outside of exterior walls and to the
centerline of common walls. In the event of any dispute as to the square feet of Rentable Area in the Premises or in the Shopping
Center, the determination of Landlord’s architect shall be binding upon the parties.
1.10
“RENTAL”: Basic Rental, Percentage Rental, Prepaid Rental, Security Deposits, Tenant’s Proportionate
Share (as defined in Paragraph 5) of the Operating Expenses (as defined in Paragraph 5), and any other sums due hereunder,
including, but not limited to Rental adjustments.
1.11
“RULES AND REGULATIONS”: Those rules and regulations which are set forth in EXHIBIT “B” to this
Lease, as amended, reduced or added to pursuant to this Lease.
1.12
“SUBSTANTIAL COMPLETION”: The Premises shall be substantially completed on the date that
Landlord’s architect reasonably determines that all work to be performed by Landlord pursuant to this Lease has been performed,
other than Punch List Items. If Landlord is not using an architect, then Landlord shall make the determination concerning
Substantial Completion, so long as Landlord’s determination is reasonable.
1.13

“TENANT DELAY”: Any delay caused by Tenant, including without limitation, any of the following:
(a)

Tenant’s failure to furnish information in accordance with the requirements of this Lease, or to
respond to any request by Landlord for any approval or information within any time period
prescribed, or if no time period is prescribed, then within two days of the request;

2.

(b)

Tenant’s insistence on materials, finishes or installation other than the standard materials, finishes
or installations provided by Landlord if Tenant has been informed by Landlord in writing, at or
before the time of delivery to Tenant of final construction pricing for Tenant’s approval, that such
materials, finishes or installations will cause a Tenant Delay;

(c)

Tenant’s changes in any plans and specifications;

(d)

Any delay in the performance by a person, firm or corporation employed by Tenant in the
completion of any work by said person, firm or corporation (all such work and such persons, firms
or corporations being subject to the approval of Landlord);

(e)

Any request by Tenant that Landlord delay the completion of any of Landlord’s Work;

(f)

Any breach or default by Tenant in the performance of Tenant’s obligations under this Lease;

(g)

LEASE TERM AND OCCUPANCY

3.1
Mid-Month Occupancy. If the Commencement Date is not the first day of a calendar month, then the Lease
Term shall be extended by the time between the Commencement Date and the first day of the next month.
3.2
Tenant Acceptance. ( a ) Tenant warrants to Landlord that it has conducted its own independent investigation
of the Premises and the Shopping Center, ( b ) Tenant agrees that the Premises and the Shopping center are suitable for the
purpose for which the Premises is leased, ( c ) except for the obligations of Landlord under Exhibit C, Tenant accepts the
Premises (including the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection and HVAC systems) and the Shopping Center, each in
its condition as of the date of this Lease and has waived any defects in any of the Premise or the Shopping Center, and ( d )
Tenant acknowledges that the Premises and the Shopping Center fully comply with Landlord’s covenants and obligations. The
provisions of this Subparagraph shall be effective whether or not a Confirmation Letter (as defined below) is provided by Tenant.
3.3
Confirmation Letter. Within ten days after request by Landlord, Tenant shall execute and deliver to Landlord
a letter (a “CONFIRMATION LETTER”) in the form of EXHIBIT “C”, confirming (i) the Commencement Date,
(ii) that Tenant has accepted the Premises, and (iii) that Landlord has performed all of its obligations with respect to the Premises.
4.

RENTAL; BOOKS AND RECORDS

4.1
Rental Payments. Tenant shall timely pay to Landlord or Landlord’s assigns, in lawful money of the United
States, the Basic Rental, Percentage Rental and all additional sums to be paid by Tenant to Landlord under Paragraph 5 or other
Paragraphs of this Lease, without demand, deduction, abatement or set off. Payment shall be made to Landlord’s Manager at the
Manager’s address, or such other address as Landlord may from time to time designate in writing to Tenant. Basic Rental,
adjusted as provide in this Lease, shall be payable monthly in advance on the first (1st) day of each month during the Lease Term
commencing on the date shown in the Basic Lease Terms. The monthly installment schedule for Basic Rental is set forth in the
Basic Lease Terms. Basic Rental and the initial estimated amount of Tenant’s Proportionate Share of Operating Expenses for
any fractional month at the beginning of the lease Term shall be prorated based on 1/365 of the current annual amounts for each
day in such a fraction. The first full monthly installment of Basic Rental and Tenant’s Proportionate Share of Operating
Expenses, plus the Basic Rental and Tenant’s Proportionate Share for any such fractional month, shall be payable at the time set
forth in the Basic Lease Terms under “PREPAID RENTAL.” All past due installments of Rental shall bear interest at the
Contract Rate from he date due until paid.
4.2 Percentage Rental Payments. Percentage Rental shall be paid in monthly installments as follows: commencing on the
Commencement Date, on or before the 15th day of each calendar month during the remainder of the Lease Term (or the calendar
month immediately following expiration or termination of the Lease Term, in the case of the last month of the Lease Term), Tenant
shall pay to Landlord a sum equal to the Percentage Rental due with respect to the preceding full or partial calendar month.
4.3 Gross Sales. The term "Gross Sales" shall mean and include the entire amount of the sales price, whether for cash or
otherwise, of all sales of merchandise (including gift and merchandise certificates), services and other receipts whatsoever of all
business conducted in or from the Premises whether by Tenant. or a subtenant, assignee, licensee, concessionaire or other occupant,
including without limitation, mail or telephone orders received or filled at the Premises, deposits not refunded to purchasers, order
taken at the Premises (although such orders may be filled elsewhere), video and other game sales, alcoholic beverage sales, "door
charges", "admission charges", "entertainment charges", lottery Sales revenue (to the extent lawful), and other similar charges,
however designated and however and by whomever collected. Each installment or credit sale shall be treated as a sale for the full
price in the month during which such sale was made, regardless of the time when Tenant shall receive payment from its customer.
Gross Sales shall not include (a) any sums collected and paid out for any sales or excise tax imposed by any duly constituted
governmental authority, including but not limited to Arkansas Alcoholic Beverage Control Board taxes, (b) the exchange of
merchandise between the stores of Tenant, if any, where such exchanges of goods or merchandise are made solely for the
convenient operation of the business of Tenant and not for the purpose of consummating a sale which has theretofore been made
at, from or upon the Premises or for the purpose or depriving Landlord of the benefit of a sale which otherwise would be made at,
in, from or upon the Premises, (c) the amount of returns to shippers or manufacturers, (d) the amount of any cash or credit refund
made upon any sale where the merchandise sold, or some part thereof, is thereafter returned by the purchaser and accepted by
Tenant, (e) sale of Tenant's fixtures which are not stock in trade, (f) any and all service charges by credit card companies and (g)
sales through vending machines.

4.4 Records of Gross Sales. Tenant and each subtenant, licensee or concessionaire occupying the Premises or part thereof
shall, in connection with all sales, utilize, in a manner reasonably satisfactory to Landlord, cash registers (or other similar manner
reasonably satisfactory to Landlord) equipped with sales continuous totals. Tenant and each subtenant, assignee, licensee or
concessionaire of Tenant shall keep in the Premises, a permanent accurate set of books and records of all sales of merchandise and
revenue derived from business conducted in the Premises, including: cash register tapes or records; sales slips; order records of
transactions with subtenants, licensees and concessionaires; shipping records; records of merchandise returned; tax reports;
banking records; and such other records as may be needed to permit an effective audit of sales. All such records shall be retained
and preserved for at least thirty-six (36) months after the end of the calendar year to which they relate, and shall be subject to
inspection and audit by Landlord and its agents at all reasonable times, and at Landlord's expense, except as provided in
subparagraph 4.8 below.
4.5 Monthly Reports of Gross Sales. On or before the fifteenth (15th) day after the expiration of the month in which the
Commencement Date occurs, and on or before the fifteenth (15th) day of each calendar month thereafter during the remainder of
the Lease Term (or the calendar month immediately following expiration or termination of the Lease Term, in the case of the last
month of the Lease Term), Tenant shall prepare and deliver to Landlord at the place then fixed for the payment of Rental, a
statement of Gross Sales during the preceding calendar month and for the calendar year to date, in such form as the Landlord may
require, certified to be correct by Tenant and bearing the signed certification of Tenant's financial officer or certified public
accountant, if any, otherwise by Tenant's bookkeeper, accompanied by legible copies of Tenant's cash register tapes, Arkansas
Alcoholic Beverage Control Board reports, sales tax reports submitted to the appropriate taxing authority, and any similar items
reasonably requested by Landlord (collectively, the "Backup Items"). Tenant shall furnish similar statements and Backup Items
for its licensees, concessionaires and subtenants, if any.
4.6 Annual Reports of Gross Sales. On or before the sixtieth (60th) day after the expiration of each calendar year during
the Lease Term and the sixtieth (60th) day after the expiration or termination of this Lease, Tenant shall deliver to Landlord at the
place last fixed for the payment of Rental a statement, certified as correct by Tenant, showing Gross Sales during the preceding
calendar year and Gross Sales during any partial calendar year covered by the Lease Term, and, requested by Landlord,
accompanied by legible copies for such period of any Backup Items not already provided to Landlord. Tenant shall furnish similar
statements for its licensees, concessionaires and subtenants, if any. In the event any provision of this Lease, or the enforcement
thereof by Landlord, requires accounting for Gross Sales and the payment of Percentage Rental for any period less than twelve
(12) months, such shorter period shall be treated as one (1) year for the purposes of an annual statement and such statement shall
be delivered to Landlord within thirty (30) days after termination of such shorter period. With each such annual statement and
each such statement for a shorter period, Tenant shall pay to Landlord any and all sums due under this Lease which then remain
unpaid for the entire period covered by such statement. All amounts by which Tenant has overpaid Percentage Rental for the
twelve month period or any such shorter period shall be reimbursed by Landlord at the end of such period.
4.7 Gross Sales Audits. In the event Landlord is not satisfied with any statement of Gross Sales submitted by Tenant,
Landlord shall have the right, at its expense, to retain an independent certified public accountant or auditor to audit any or all books
and records, wherever located, pertaining to sales made in or from the Premises. If Tenant's statements are found to be incorrect
to an extent of more than four percent (4%) over the figures submitted by Tenant, or if Tenant has failed to timely deliver
statements, Tenant shall pay for such audit. Tenant shall promptly pay to Landlord any deficiency or Landlord shall promptly
refund Tenant any overpayment, as the case may be, which is established by such audit.
4.8 Gross Sales Reports Not Prepared bv Tenant. If Tenant, after written request from Landlord, fails to prepare and deliver
promptly any monthly, annual or other statement concerning Gross Sales or Percentage Rental which is required under this Lease,
Landlord may, at Tenant's expense, in addition to exercising any of the remedies provided to Landlord under this Lease, or at law,
make an audit of all books and records, including Tenant's bank accounts, which in any way pertain to or show Gross Sales, and to
prepare the statement or statements which Tenant failed to prepared and deliver. Such audit, if made, and such statement or
statements, if prepared by an independent certified public accountant, shall be conclusive against Tenant.
5.

ADJUSTMENT OF RENTAL

5.1
Tenant’s Proportionate Share. During the Lease Term, Tenant agrees to pay Tenant’s Proportionate Share of
Operating Expenses of the Shopping Center.
5.2
Determining Operating Expenses. The term “Operating Expenses” shall mean all expenses, costs and
disbursements of every kind and character, subject to the limitations set forth below, which Landlord shall pay in connection with
the ownership, management, operation, repair, maintenance and security of the Shopping Center, including, without limitation,
the following:
(a)

wages, salaries and fees of all personnel or entities (exclusive of Landlord’s executive personnel)
engaged in the operation, management, repair, replacement, maintenance or monitoring of the
Shopping Center, including taxes, insurance and benefits relating thereto; provided however, that if
during the Lease Term such personnel or entities are working on other projects operated by
Landlord as well as working on the Shopping Center, their wages, salaries, fees and related
expenses shall be appropriately allocated among all of such projects and only those portions of such
expenses reasonably allocable to the Shopping Center shall be included as Operating Expenses;

(b)

all supplies and materials used in the operation, ownership, management, repair, replacement,
maintenance and monitoring of the Shopping Center;

(c)

cost of all maintenance, repair, replacement, monitoring, lighting, painting, parking lot re-striping,
security, service and leasing agreements for the Shopping Center, including, without limitation, if
applicable, monitoring service, janitorial service, security, trash removal service, pest control
service, window cleaning, elevator maintenance, landscaping, lawn irrigation service, and parking
area maintenance. Tenant further agrees that, although the roof(s) of the building(s) in the
Shopping Center are not literally part of the Common Area, roof maintenance and repair shall be
included;

(d)

cost of all insurance relating to the Shopping Center, or which Landlord considers reasonably
necessary, or which is required by any Landlord’s Mortgagee (as later defined), including, without
limitation, the cost of casualty and liability insurance applicable to the Shopping Center and
Landlord’s equipment, fixtures and personal property used in connection therewith, and the cost of
business interruption insurance in such amounts as will reimburse Landlord for all losses of
earnings and other income attributable to such perils as are commonly insured against by prudent
landlords.

(e)

all Taxes. The term “TAXES” shall mean all taxes, assessments (whether general or special) and

other governmental charges, whether federal, state, county or municipal, and whether assessed by
taxing districts or authorities presently taxing the Shopping Center or by others, subsequently
created or otherwise, and any sales taxes, use taxes or other taxes and assessments attributable to
the Shopping Center, the property upon which it is located and the buildings and other
improvements comprising the Shopping Center, or its rental and operation, exclusive of any
inheritance, gift, franchise, income, corporate or profit taxes which may be assessed against
Landlord. If the present method of taxation changes so that in lieu of the whole or any part of any
Taxes levied on the Shopping Center, there is levied on Landlord a capital tax directly on the rents
received therefrom or a franchise tax, assessment, or charge based, in whole or in part, upon such
rents for the Shopping Center, then all such taxes, assessments, or charges or the part hereof so
based, shall be included within the term “Taxes”;
(f)

cost of repairs, replacements, general maintenance, and compliance with present and future laws
and regulations relating to the Common Areas, and cost of legal expenses and related costs incurred
for the general benefit of the tenants of the Shopping Center (e.g. legal fees and consultant fees in
property tax disputes);

(g)

annual cost of all capital improvements made to the Common Areas ( i ) which although capital in
nature can reasonably be expected to reduce the normal operating costs of the Common Areas, (II)
in order to comply with the ADA or any other law or regulation that was not applicable to the
Common Areas when originally constructed or any law or regulation that is hereafter promulgated
by any governmental authority relating to energy, conservation, public safety or security, or ( III )
which enhance the Common Areas for the general benefit of tenants or occupants thereof, as
amortized over the useful economic life of such improvements as determined by Landlord in its
reasonable discretion, without regard tot he period of such improvements as determined by
Landlord in its reasonable discretion, without regard to the period over which such improvements
may be depreciated or amortized for federal income tax purposes;

(h)

all charges for utilities to the Common Areas, including, but not limited to, water, sewer, electricity
and gas, which are paid by Landlord;

(i)

the management fee which is from time to time in effect and which is due to the manager of the
Shopping Center; and

(j)

rent of Landlord’s management offices on or adjacent to the Shopping Center, or its fair rental
value.

The following costs are specifically excluded from the definition of the term “Operating Expenses”:
( i ) capital improvements made to the Shopping center except (A) capital improvements described in
subparagraph 5.2(g) above and (B) items which, though capital for accounting purposes, are properly
considered maintenance and repair items, such as painting of the Common Area; ( ii ) repair, replacements
and general maintenance paid by proceeds of insurance or by Tenant or other third parties, and alterations
attributable solely to tenants of the Shopping Center other than Tenant; (iii) for interest, amortization or other
payments on loans to Landlord; (iv) for depreciation of the Shopping center; (v) for leasing commissions; (vi)
for legal expenses, other than those incurred for the general benefit of the tenants of the Shopping Center
(e.g., tax disputes); (vii) for renovating or otherwise improving space for occupants of the Shopping Center or
vacant space in the Shopping Center; and (viii) for federal income taxes imposed on or measured by the
income of Landlord from the operation of the Shopping Center.
5.3
Making Expense Payments. Landlord may collect Tenant’s Proportionate Share of the Operating Expenses
(the “EXPENSE PAYMENT”) in a lump sum annually, to be due within 30 days after Landlord furnishes to Tenant the Annual
Share Statement (as defined below). Alternatively, Landlord may make a good faith estimate of the Expense Payment to be due
by Tenant for any calendar year or part thereof during the Lease Term. Unless Landlord delivers to Tenant a revision of the
estimated Expense Payment, Tenant shall pay to Landlord, on the Commencement Date and on the first day of each calendar
month thereafter, an amount equal to the estimated Expense Payment for such calendar year or part thereof divided by the
number of months in such calendar year during the Lease Term. From time to time during any calendar year, Landlord may
estimate and re-estimate the Expense Payment to be due by Tenant for that calendar year and deliver a copy of the estimate or reestimate to Tenant. Thereafter, the monthly installments of Expense Payment payable by Tenant shall be appropriately adjusted
in accordance with the estimations so that, by the end of the calendar year in questions, Tenant shall have paid all of the Expense
Payment as estimated by Landlord. Any amounts paid based on such an estimate shall be subject to adjustment pursuant to
Subparagraph 5.4 when actual Operating Expenses are available for each calendar year. Until Tenant has received the estimate
form Landlord, Tenant shall continue to pay Expense Payments in the same amount, if any, as required for the last month of the
prior calendar year. If the Commencement Date of this Lease is not the first day of a calendar year, or the expiration or
termination date of this Lease is not the last day of a calendar year, then the Expense Payment shall be prorated. The foregoing
adjustment provisions shall survive the termination of this Lease.
5.4
Annual Share Statement. By April 1 of each calendar year, or as soon thereafter as practicable, Landlord
shall furnish to Tenant a statement (the “ANNUAL SHARE STATEMENT”) showing the amounts Tenant paid as estimated
Expense Payments, compared to the actual Expense Payment which should have been paid for the previous year, calculated and
adjusted as provided in Subparagraph 5.2. If the Annual Share Statement reveals that Tenant paid more than the actual Expense
Payment in the year for which such statement was prepared, then Landlord shall promptly credit or reimburse Tenant such
excess; likewise, if Tenant paid less than the actual Expense Payment, then Tenant shall promptly pay Landlord such deficiency.
5.5
Books and Records for Operating Expenses. Landlord, upon Tenant’s written request, will provide Tenant
with an annual statement reflecting the Operating Expenses of the Shopping center for any year (or partial year, as the case may
be) during the Lease Term, or any renewal or extension thereof. Landlord agrees to keep books and records showing Operating
Expenses, using a system of accounts and accounting practices consistently maintained on a year-to-year basis, in accordance
with accepted accounting practices. For a period of two years after the period such books and records relate to, Landlord agrees
to make such books and records available to Tenant for inspection at Landlord’s office at reasonable times which are convenient
to Landlord.
6.

DELINQUENT PAYMENT; HANDLING CHARGES

All payments required of Tenant hereunder shall bear interest from the date due until paid at the Contract Rate. In
addition, Landlord may charge Tenant a fee equal to 4% of the delinquent payment to reimburse Landlord for its cost and
inconvenience incurred as a consequence of Tenant’s delinquency. In no event, however, shall the charges permitted under this
Paragraph or elsewhere in this Lease, to the extent the same are considered to be interest under applicable law, exceed the
maximum lawful rate of interest. If Tenant pays Rental but such payment is not made in a timely manner, without waiving any
other rights of Landlord, Landlord may declare the same to be an Event of Default or may require Tenant to pay Rental on or
before the due date in cash, or by cashier’s check or money order, and the delivery of Tenant’s collectible personal or corporate
check shall no longer constitute payment. Any acceptance of Tenant’s personal or corporate check thereafter by Landlord shall
not be construed as a waiver of the requirement that such payments be made in cash or by cashier’s check or money order.
7.

SECURITY DEPOSIT

Tenant shall pay to Landlord a Security Deposit in the amount specified in the Basic Lease Terms. The Security
Deposit shall be paid at the time specified in the Basic Lease Terms. The Security Deposit shall be held by Landlord without
liability for interest and as security for the performance by Tenant of its obligations under this Lease. Landlord may commingle
such deposit with any other funds held by Landlord. The Security Deposit is not an advance payment of Rental or a measure or
limit of Landlord’s damages upon an Event of Default (as defined below). Landlord may, from time to time and without
prejudice to any other remedy, use all or a part of the Security Deposit to perform any obligation which Tenant was obligated
under this Lease to perform and did not perform, including without limitation, paying any Rental due and paying for any damage,
injury, expense or liability caused to Landlord by Tenant’s failure to perform. Following any such application of the Security
Deposit, Tenant shall pay to Landlord on demand the amount so applied in order to restore the Security Deposit to its original
amount. Within a reasonable time after the Lease Term ends, provided Tenant has performed all of its obligations under this
Lease, Landlord shall return to Tenant the balance of the Security Deposit which has not been applied to satisfy Tenant’s
obligations. If Landlord transfers its interest in the Premises, then Landlord may assign the Security Deposit to the transferee and
landlord thereafter shall have no further liability for the return of the Security Deposit.
8.

UTILITIES

8.1
Utilities. Landlord agrees to cause to be provided the necessary mains, conduits and other facilities necessary
to supply water, gas (if deemed appropriate by Landlord), electricity, telephone service and sewerage service to the building in
which the Premises are located. Tenant acknowledges that the existing capacities of such utility services are adequate for the
intended operation of the Permitted Use and Landlord shall have no duty or obligation to supply any utility services in excess of
such quantities. Tenant further agrees not to use the Premises in any manner which would require utility service in excess of
such quantities.
8.2
Tenant Payment . Tenant shall promptly pay all charges for electricity, water, gas, telephone services,
sewerage service and other utilities furnished to the Premises. Landlord may, if it so elects, furnish one or more utility services to
Tenant, and in such event Tenant shall purchase the use and quantity of such services as are tendered by Landlord, and shall pay
on demand as Rental, rates established therefore by Landlord which shall not exceed the rates which would be charged for the
same services if furnished directly by the local public utility companies. Landlord may at any time discontinue furnishing any
service which is then being provided by Landlord without liability or obligation to Tenant other than to connect the Premises to
the local public utility, if any, furnishing such service.
8.3
Restoration of Services; Abatement. Landlord shall not be liable for any interruption whatsoever in utility
services not furnished by Landlord, nor for interruptions in utility services furnished by Landlord which are due to fire, accident,
strike, any force majeure described in subparagraph 27.3, or any other cause beyond the control of Landlord or in order to make
alterations, repairs or improvements to the Premises, the building in which the Premises is located or the Shopping Center.
Landlord shall use reasonable efforts to restore any utility service which becomes unavailable, if the service is provided by
Landlord, if the restoration is within the reasonable control of Landlord, and if the interruption was caused in whole or substantial
part by the gross negligence of Landlord. If the interruption was caused in whole or substantial part by Tenant or any of its
agents, contractors, employees or customers, then at Landlord’s request, Tenant shall promptly pay Landlord all reasonable
amounts estimated by Landlord as necessary to restore any service. Upon receipt of such amounts, Landlord shall use reasonable
efforts to restore such service to the extent such restoration is within the reasonable control of Landlord. Landlord agrees to
promptly account for the actual amount of restoration costs and damages due to such interruption caused in whole or substantial
part by Tenant, after which Landlord shall pay Tenant any excess of such estimated payment over the actual amount of
restoration costs and damages, or Tenant shall pay Landlord any excess of the actual amount of restoration costs and damages
over such estimated payment. Whether or not Tenant or Landlord is at fault, any unavailability, stoppage or interruption of such
services shall not render Landlord liable for any damages caused thereby, shall not be an actual or constructive eviction of
Tenant, shall not constitute a breach of this Lease or any implied warranty, and shall not entitle Tenant to any abatement,
recoupment or set off of Tenant’s Rental or reduction or elimination of Tenant’s other obligations hereunder. Landlord may
interrupt or stop any services when reasonably needed for emergencies, repairs and maintenance and shall not thereby be deemed
negligent or willful or in violation of this Lease, so long as Landlord uses reasonable diligence to resume such interrupted or
stopped services thereafter. Inconvenience to Tenant shall not cause the Premises to be uninhabitable. The Premises is
uninhabitable under this Lease only during the time that the Tenant is deprived of the use and benefit of substantially all of the
Premises due to the interruption.
9.

COMMON AREA

The Common Area shall be subject to Landlord’s sole management and control and shall be operated and maintained in
such manner as Landlord in Landlord’s discretion shall determine. Landlord reserves the right to change from time to time the
dimensions, level, arrangement, characteristics and location of the Shopping Center or any Common Areas, and to place,
construct or erect new, or remove, structures or other improvements (including elevated or double-deck parking facilities and/or
additional retail buildings or additional levels to existing retail buildings) on any part of the Shopping Center or any Common
Areas without the consent of Tenant. Those parts of the Common Area which Tenant may be permitted to use are used under a
revocable license. If the facilities and the size of the Common Area are diminished, Landlord shall not be subject to any liability,
Tenant shall not be entitled to any compensation or abatement of Rental, and the diminution of the Common Area shall not be
deemed constructive or actual eviction.
Tenant, and its employees and customers, and when expressly authorized pursuant to the provisions of this Lease, its
subtenants, licensees and concessionaires, shall have the nonexclusive right to use the Common Area (excluding roofs of
buildings in the Shopping Center) as constituted from time to time, such use to be in common with Landlord, other tenants in the
Shopping Center and other persons permitted by the Landlord to use the same, and subject to such reasonable rules and
regulations governing use as Landlord from time to time shall prescribe. For example, and without limiting the generality of

Landlord’s ability to establish rules and regulations governing all aspects of the Common Area, Tenant agrees as follows:

10.

(a)

Landlord may from time to time designate specific areas within the Shopping Center or in reasonable
proximity thereto where automobiles owned by Tenant, its employees, subtenants, licensees and
concessionaires shall be parked; and in this regard, Tenant shall furnish to Landlord upon request, a complete
list of license numbers of all automobiles operated by Tenant, its employees, subtenants, licensees and
concessionaires, and Tenant agrees that if any automobile or other vehicle owned by Tenant or any of its
employees, subtenants, licensees or concessionaires shall at any time be parked in any part of the Shopping
Center other than the specified areas designated for employee parking, Tenant shall pay to Landlord as
additional rent upon demand an amount equal to the daily rate or charge for such parking established by
Landlord from time to time for each day, or part thereof, such automobile or other vehicle is so parked.

(b)

Tenant and its subtenants, licensees and concessionaires shall not conduct or solicit business (such as, but not
limited to, distribution of handbills or leaflets) within the Common Area nor take any action which would
interfere with the rights of other persons to use the Common Area.

(c)

Landlord may temporarily close any part of the Common Area for such periods of time as may be necessary
to make repairs or alterations or to prevent the public from obtaining prescriptive rights.

(d)

With regard to the roof(s) of the building(s) in the Shopping Center, use of the roof(s) is reserved to Landlord
or, with regard to any tenant demonstrating to Landlord’s satisfaction a need to same, to such tenant after
receiving prior written consent from Landlord, which may be withheld in Landlord’s sole discretion.

(e)

Landlord shall have the right to permit entertainment events, placement of kiosks, advertising and other
displays or promotional events in the Common Areas, whether on a temporary or permanent basis. Landlord
shall be responsible for the operation, management and maintenance of the Common Area, the manner of
maintenance and the expenditures therefore to be in the sole discretion of Landlord, but to be generally in
keeping with similar shopping centers within the same geographical area as the Shopping Center.

IMPROVEMENTS; ALTERATIONS; REPAIRS; MAINTENANCE

10.1
Improvements; Alterations. Tenant shall not make any alterations, additions or improvements to the
Premises without the prior written consent of Landlord, except for the installation of unattached, movable trade fixtures which
may be installed without drilling cutting or otherwise defacing the premises. Without limiting the generality of the immediately
preceding sentence, any installation or replacement of heating or air conditions equipment must be effected strictly in accordance
with Landlord’s instructions. Tenant and tenant’s agents, employees, contractors and invitees shall not appoint or install lighting
or decoration, signs, window or door lettering, or advertising media of any type on or about the Premises, without the prior
written consent of Landlord. Tenant and Tenant’s agents, employees, contractors and invitees shall not deface or injure the
Premises, in any manner. All temporary or permanent alterations, additions, replacements or improvements (other than
unattached, readily movable trade fixtures, signs and equipment) which are in or upon the Premises, including without limitation
any installed by or for Landlord or Tenant, and any air conditioning equipment, and any equipment that is in any manner
connected to the plumbing system, shall be Landlord’s property at the end of the Lease Term, and shall remain on the premises
without compensation to Tenant. Landlord has made no representation as to the condition of the Premises, nor has Landlord
agreed to remodel, repair or decorate, except as expressly set forth in Exhibit “C” attached to this Lease. Notwithstanding
anything in this Lease to the contrary, Tenant shall be responsible for the cost of all work required to comply with the retrofit
requirements of the ADA if such work is necessitated by Tenant’s use of the Premises or necessitated by any installations,
additions, or alterations made in or to the Premises by Tenant or at the request of Tenant, regardless of whether such cost is
incurred in connection with retrofit work required in the Premises or in other areas of the Shopping Center.
10.2
Repairs; Maintenance. Landlord shall keep the foundation, the exterior walls (except plate glass, windows,
doors, door closure devices and other exterior openings, window and door frames, molding, locks and hardware, special store
fronts, lighting, heating, air conditioning, plumbing and other electrical, mechanical and electromotive installation, equipment
and fixtures, signs, placards, decorations or other advertising media of any type, and interior painting or other treatment of
exterior walls [collectively “Wall Items”]) and roof (subject to the inclusion of such costs in Operating Expenses) of the Premises
in good repair. Landlord, however, shall not be required to make any repairs occasioned by the act or negligence of Tenant, its
agents, employees, subtenants, licensees and concessionaires (including, but not limited to, roof leaks resulting from Tenant’s
installation of air conditioning equipment or any other roof penetration or placement, without implying Landlord’s consent
thereto); and the provisions of the previous sentence are expressly recognized to be subject to the provisions of Article 16 and
Article 17 of this Lease. In the event that the Premises should become in need of repairs required to be made by Landlord
hereunder, Tenant shall give immediate written notice thereof to Landlord; and landlord shall not be responsible in any way for
failure to make any such repairs until a reasonable time shall have elapsed after receipt by Landlord of such written notice.
Except where the same is caused by Landlord’s gross negligence or intentional acts, Landlord shall not be liable to Tenant for
any damage to merchandise, trade fixtures or personal property in the Premises caused by water leakage from roof, water lines,
sprinklers or heating and air conditioning equipment.
Tenant shall keep all areas of the Premises (including, but not limited to, the Wall items) in good, clean and
habitable condition and shall at its sole cost and expense keep the Premises free of insects, rodents, vermin and other pests
(unless Landlord elects to include pest control as a central Operating Expense of the Shopping Center) and make all needed
repairs and replacements, including replacement of cracked or broken glass, except for repairs and replacements required to be
made by Landlord under the provision of this Section 10.2, Article 16 or Article 17. Without limiting the coverage of the
previous sentence, it is understood that Tenant’s responsibilities therein include the repair and replacement of all lighting,
heating, air conditioning, plumbing, and other electrical, mechanical and electromotive installation, equipment and fixtures and
also include all utility repairs in ducts, conduits, pipes and wiring, and any sewer stoppage located in, under and above the
Premises. If any repairs required to be made by Tenant hereunder are not made within ten days after written notice delivered to
Tenant by Landlord, Landlord may at its option make such repairs without liability to Tenant for any loss or damage which may
result to its stock or business by reason of such repairs, and Tenant shall pay to Landlord upon demand, as Rental hereunder, the
cost of such repairs plus interest at the Contract Rate, such interest to accrue continuously from the date of payment by Landlord
until repayment by Tenant. At the expiration of this Lease, Tenant shall surrender the Premises in good condition, excepting
reasonable wear and tear and losses required to be restored by Landlord in this Section 10.2, Article 16 and Article 17 of this
Lease.

10.3
Performance of Work. All construction work done by Tenant within the Premises shall be performed in a
good and workmanlike manner, shall be diligently prosecuted to completion, in compliance with all governmental requirements,
and in such manner as to cause a minimum of interference with other construction in progress and with the transaction of
business in the Shopping Center. Tenant agrees to indemnify and defend Landlord and hold Landlord harmless against any loss,
liability, expense (including attorneys’ fees) or damage resulting from such work, and Tenant shall, if requested by Landlord,
furnish bond or other security satisfactory to Landlord against any such loss, liability or damage. Tenant shall cause all
contractors and subcontractors to procure and maintain insurance coverage against such risks, in such amounts, and with such
companies as Landlord may reasonably require, and to procure payment and performance bonds reasonably satisfactory to
Landlord covering the cost of the work. All such work shall be performed in accordance with all legal requirements (including,
without limitation, obtaining all required permits, inspections and certificates of occupancy) and in a good and workmanlike
manner so as not to damage the Premises, or otherwise damage or alter the primary structure, structural qualities and other
aspects of the building where the Premise is located, or plumbing, electrical lines, or other utility transmission facilities. All such
work which may affect the HVAC, electrical system, any structural components of the Premises or the building where the
Premises is located, any building central systems, the roof to the Premises or plumbing must be approved (which may be
withheld in Landlord’s sole and absolute discretion) by Landlord in writing and, as a condition to the performance of any such
work, Landlord may require that Landlord’s contractor perform such work in which event Tenant shall be responsible for
payment of such work. Approval by Landlord of any drawings, plans and specifications, engineering plans or other items
prepared in connection with any improvements in the Premises shall not constitute a representation or warranty of Landlord as to
the compliance with the ADA or their applicable laws, rules and regulations, or the adequacy, completeness, or design
sufficiency for any use, purpose, or condition, of such drawings, plans , specifications, engineering plans or other items, or the
improvements to which they relate. Landlord approval shall merely be the consent of Landlord as required hereunder.
10.4
No Liens. Tenant shall not permit creation or filing against the Premises, or the Shopping Center, of any lien
or encumbrance of any type which secures or arises from any debt or obligation of Tenant, including but not limited to any
statutory liens for any work performed, materials furnished, or obligations incurred by or at the request of Tenant. If such a lien is
created or filed, then Tenant shall, within ten days after Landlord has delivered notice of the same to Tenant, either pay the
amount of the lien, cause the lien to be fully released or diligently contest the lien and deliver to Landlord a bond which will
prevent foreclosure of the subject property or other security reasonably satisfactory to Landlord a bond which will prevent
foreclosure of the subject property or other security reasonably satisfactory to Landlord. If Tenant fails to timely take either such
action, then, without limitation to Landlord’s other remedies under this Lease, Landlord may pay the lien claims without inquiry
as to the validity thereof, and any amounts so paid, including expenses, attorneys’ fees and interest at the Contract Rate, shall be
paid by Tenant to Landlord within ten days after Landlord has delivered an invoice to Tenant.
10.5
Inconvenience. In the event that Landlord elects to remodel all or any portion of the Shopping Center,
Tenant will cooperate with such remodeling, including Tenant’s tolerating temporary inconveniences (and even the temporary
removal of Tenant’s signs in order to facilitate such remodeling, as it may relate to the exterior of the Premises).
11.

USE; TENANT’S OBLIGATIONS

11.1
General Use. Tenant shall continuously occupy and use the Premises only for the Permitted Use under the
Trade Name. Tenant shall comply at Tenant’s expense with all laws, orders, rules and regulations including zoning, building and
fire code regulations, relating to the use, condition, and occupancy of the Premises. The Premises shall not be used for any use
which is disreputable or creates extraordinary fire hazards or results in a cancellation or an increased rate of insurance on the
Shopping Center or its contents, or for the storage of any hazardous material or substances. The Premises shall not be used for
or in conjunction with any illegal activity. If, because of the acts or Tenant’s agents, employees or invitees, the rate of insurance
on the Shopping center or its contents increases, then such acts shall be an Event of Default, Tenant shall pay to Landlord the
amount of such increase on demand, and acceptance of such payment shall not constitute a waiver of any of Landlord’s other
rights. Tenant shall conduct its business and control its agents, employees, contractors and invitees in such a manner as: not to
create any nuisance or interfere with other tenants or Landlord in its management and operation of the Shopping Center; not to
commit any act which might damage Landlord’s or the Shopping Center’s goodwill or reputation, or tend to injure or depreciate
the Shopping Center; not to commit or permit waste or damage in the Premises or the Shopping Center; and not store any items
outside the Premises. All personal property belonging to Tenant or any occupant of the Premises or any other person, and located

for this restriction is the maintenance of a first-class shopping center image, not price regulation; therefore, Landlord agrees that

applicable laws and maintains an image consistent with the remainder of the Shopping Center.

respective premises; nor permit any unlawful or immoral practice to be carried on or committed on the Premises; nor do anything
which would tend to injure the reputation of the Shopping Center.

FIRE OR OTHER CASUALTY

within sixty (60) days after such Casualty, deliver to Tenant a good faith estimate (the “DAMAGE NOTICE”) of the time needed
to repair the damage caused by such Casualty.
17.2
Landlord’s and Tenant’s Rights. If material portion of the Premises or the building in which the Premises is
located is damaged by Casualty not caused in whole or material part by Tenant, and Tenant is prevented from conducting its
business in the Premises in a manner reasonably comparable to that conducted immediately before such Casualty, and Landlord
estimates that the damage caused thereby cannot be repaired with 180 days after the commencement of repair, then Landlord or

Tenant may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice to the other party of its election to terminate within thirty (30) days
after the Damage Notice has been delivered to Tenant. If neither Landlord nor Tenant elects to terminate this Lease, or if
Landlord estimates that the damage can be repaired in less than 180 days after the commencement of repair, then (subject to

17.3
Landlord’s Rights. If a Casualty damages all or a material portion of the Premises, the building in which the
Premises is located or the Shopping Center, and Landlord makes a good faith determination that restoring the Premises or such
other area would be uneconomical, or if Landlord is required to pay any insurance proceeds arising out of the Casualty to

within thirty (30) days after the Damage Notice has been delivered to Tenant, and Basic Rental hereunder shall be apportioned as

Repair Obligation. If neither party elects to terminate this Lease following a Casualty, then Landlord shall,
within a reasonable time after such Casualty, commence to repair the Premises and the Common Area, and shall proceed with
reasonable diligence to restore the Premises and the Common Area, to substantially the same condition as they existed
immediately before such Casualty; however, Landlord shall not be required to repair or replace any part of the furniture,
equipment, fixtures, and other improvements which may have been placed in the Premises by, or at the request of, Tenant or
other occupants of the Premises, and Landlord’s obligation to repair or restore the Premises or Common Area shall be limited to

Landlord’s Mortgagee. If Landlord repairs or rebuilds the Premises as provided herein, Tenant shall repair and replace its
merchandise, trade fixtures, furnishings and equipment in a manner and to at least a condition equal to that prior to the Casualty.
Landlord shall not be liable for any inconvenience or annoyance to Tenant or injury tot he business of Tenant resulting in any
way from such damage or repair and Tenant agrees to use reasonable efforts to continue the operation of its business at the
Premises during the period of any repair or restoration.

PURPOSE
This handbook provides for Cabot Fire Department (CFD) organization, administration, and
operation. It serves to identify minimum standards for all members of this department and to
help ensure fairness to all members at any rank. All firefighters will become familiar with and
be held accountable for the provisions herein. General or special orders and operating
procedures issued hereafter relating to the operations, duties, or discipline of firefighters shall be
recognized and considered as part of this handbook. All CFD employees will sign an
acknowledgement of receipt and agreement to abide by the Cabot City Employee Handbook, this
Cabot Fire Department Employee Handbook, and each amendment thereafter. Penalties for nonadherence to CFD Policies and Procedures are contained in subsequent paragraphs and/or the
City of Cabot Employee Handbook available in the Human Resources Office and on file in the
City Clerk’s Office.
MISSION STATEMENT
The mission of the Cabot Fire Department is to provide an umbrella of security for our citizens
by minimizing the loss of life and property resulting from fires, medical and environmental
emergencies, and other disasters.

CODE OF ETHICS
Background
The Fire Service is a noble calling, one which is founded on mutual respect and trust between
firefighters and the citizens they serve. To ensure the continuing integrity of the fire service, the
highest standards of ethical conduct must be maintained at all times.
The purpose of this National Firefighter Code of Ethics is to establish criterion that encourage
fire service personnel to promote a culture of ethical integrity and high standards of
professionalism in our field. The broad scope of this Code of Ethics is intended to mitigate and
negate situations that may result in embarrassment and waning of public support for what has
historically been a highly respected profession.
Ethics comes from the Greek word ethos, meaning character. Character is not necessarily
defined by how a person behaves when conditions are optimal and life is good. It is easy to take
the high road when the path is paved and obstacles are few or non-existent. Character is also
defined by decisions made under pressure, when no one is looking, when the road contains land
9

mines, and the way is obscured. As members of the fire service, we share a responsibility to
project an ethical character of professionalism, integrity, compassion, loyalty, and honesty in all
that we do, all of the time.
We need to accept this ethics challenge and be truly willing to maintain a culture that is
consistent with the expectations outlined in this document. By doing so, we can create a legacy
that validates and sustains the distinguished fire service institution, and at the same time ensure
that we leave the fire service in better condition than when we arrived.
Fire Fighter Code of Ethics
I understand that I have the responsibility to conduct myself in a manner that reflects
proper ethical behavior and integrity. In so doing, I will help foster a continuing positive
public perception of the fire service. Therefore, I pledge the following:


Conduct myself, on and off duty, in a manner that reflects positively on me, my
department, and the fire service in general.



Accept responsibility for my actions and for the consequences of my actions.



Support the concept of fairness and the value of diverse thoughts and opinions.



Avoid situations that would adversely affect the credibility or public perception of the
fire service profession



Be truthful and honest at all times and report instances of cheating or other dishonest acts
that compromise the integrity of the fire service.



Conduct my personal affairs in a manner that does not improperly influence the
performance of my duties, or bring discredit to my organization.



Be respectful and conscious of each member’s safety and welfare.



Recognize that I serve in a position of public trust that requires stewardship in the honest
and efficient use of publicly owned resources, including uniforms, facilities, vehicles, and
equipment and that these are protected from misuse and theft.



Exercise professionalism, competence, respect, and loyalty in the performance of my
duties and use information confidential or otherwise, gained by virtue of my position,
only to benefit those I am entrusted to serve.



Avoid financial investments, outside employment, outside business interests, or activates
that conflict with or are enhanced by my official position or have the potential to create
the perception of impropriety.

10



Neither propose nor accept personal rewards, special privileges, benefits, advancement,
honors, or gifts that may create a conflict of interest or the appearance thereof.



If I choose to drink alcohol, I will do so in a responsible way that will not affect my
mental state in such a way that my judgment is impaired, the performance of my duties
suffers, or safety is compromised.



Never discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, creed, age, marital status, national
origin, ancestry, gender, sexual preference, medical condition, or handicap.



Not intentionally harass, intimidate, or threaten fellow members of the service or the
public, and stop or report the actions of other firefighters who engage in such behaviors.



Responsibly use social networking, electronic communications, or other media
technology opportunities in a manner that does not discredit, dishonor, or embarrass my
organization, the fire service, or the public. I also understand that failure to resolve or
report inappropriate use of this media equates to condoning this behavior.

1. SECTION I – GENERAL POLICIES
1.1. Policy #1 – Organization: The Cabot Fire Department (CFD) shall consist of a Fire
Chief as appointed by the Mayor of Cabot. The Fire Chief may then structure the CFD chain
of command within the confines of the annual budget approved by the Cabot City Council.
The chain of command may include, but is not limited to, assistant chief(s), battalion chief(s),
division chief(s). captain(s), lieutenant(s), engineersdriver(s), and firefighters. All uniformed
personnel within the chain of command will be responsible for the following major functions:
1.1.1. Fire Prevention: the prevention of fires through programs, presentations, inspections,
pre-planning, and enforcement of the adopted Fire Prevention Code.
1.1.2. Fire Suppression: the extinguishment of fire and the conservation of life and property
in the event of fire or other emergency.
1.1.3. Basic Life Support: basic lifesaving procedures such as artificial ventilation and cardio
pulmonary resuscitation.
1.1.4. Rescue Operations: removal of individuals from situations hazardous to their health
and/or safety.
1.2. Policy #2 – Authority
1.2.1. The Fire Chief is appointed by the mayor and is the commanding officer of the CFD.
He has the authority to take appropriate actions to exercise his duties in the areas of fire
prevention, fire suppression, or other threat to life or property from fire, hazardous materials,
explosion, or other emergency. In addition to those duties imposed by ordinances, he will
perform the following:
1.2.1.1. Enforce compliance with this handbook.
1.2.1.2. The uniformed force of the CFD, with the exception of those designated by the Fire
Chief, shall be divided into three shifts, which shall perform duty of alternate shifts as now
provided by law and ordinances. The hours worked shall be left to the discretion of the Fire
Chief within the limits of the law.
1.2.1.3. Take action deemed necessary for the maintenance of discipline and order in the CFD.
1.2.1.4. Appoint qualified members to positions within the CFD provided by these policies.
1.2.1.5. Promote, demote, detail, suspend, or recommend termination of members of the CFD.
1.2.1.6. Answer to the governing body of Cabot for proper management and operation of the
CFD.

12

The Assistant Fire Chief ranks next below the Fire Chief.
The Assistant Fire Chief is second in command and shall assume the Fire Chief’s duties and
responsibilities during the absence of the Fire Chief.
The Assistant Fire Chief is charged with enforcement of the Policies and Procedures; the
supervision and control of the fire suppression force in the absence of, or as directed by, the
Fire Chief; and the inspection of stations, apparatus, tools, and equipment to assure proper
condition and maintenance.
The Assistant Fire Chief(s) will perform such other duties as the Fire Chief may direct.
1.2.2. Battalion Chief ranks next below the Assistant Fire Chief.
1.2.2.1. The Battalion Chief is second third in command and shall assume the Assistant Fire
Chief’s duties and responsibilities during the absence of the Assistant Fire Chief.
1.2.2.2. A Battalion Chief directly supervises multiple crews and participates in fire
suppression, fire prevention, rescue, and basic life-saving emergency medical response in the
city while assisting the fire chief in strategic planning for those activities.
1.2.2.3. Provides support and feedback to the fire chief to ensure positive morale and
continuous improvement in the fire department.
1.2.2.4. Provides input to the fire chief for the development of long-range plans to meet
emergency response and fire prevention needs in the city.
1.2.2.5. Advises the fire chief on gaps between fire department capabilities and Insurance
Services Office requirements.
1.2.2.6. Provides quality training and education opportunities for assigned crews ensuring
continuous improvement in department emergency response readiness and prevention
programs.
1.2.2.7. Hold assigned crews accountable for guidance provided in fire department and city
handbooks and by the fire chief and assistant fire chief.
1.2.2.8. Provides the fire chief with input for preparation of annual and strategic budgeting.
1.2.2.9. Responds to multi-company incident scenes, as the incident commander, to direct
activities of assigned fire crews, and adheres to the National Incident Management System.
1.2.2.10. Proficient in the use of spreadsheet, presentation, word processing, incident
reporting, and time accounting software.

13

1.2.2.11. Ensure the physical and mental fitness of assigned crews. Identify potential gaps to
the fire chief.
1.2.2.12. Coordinate with assistant fire chief to ensure proper staffing for assigned crews.
1.2.2.13. Performs firefighter duties and basic life support as required.
1.2.2.14. Prepares and reviews incident reports for accuracy and completeness.
1.2.2.15. Inspects structures damaged by fire or other disaster to determine safety of the
structure.
1.2.2.16. Enforces proper facility, equipment, and apparatus maintenance for fire department
property.
1.2.2.17. All other duties as assigned by the fire chief.
1.2.3. Division Chief is of equal rank to Battalion Chief and serves as an administrative staff
to the fire chief.
1.2.4. Company Officers (Captains) rank next below the Battalion Chief. Company Officers
shall rank by date of appointment with Captains ranking above Engineers or as otherwise
directed by the Fire Chief.
1.2.4.1. Company Officers will ensure required daily training is conducted and documented
each shift.
1.2.4.2. Company Officers will ensure that all matters of safety receive top priority and focus
during all operations.
1.2.4.3. Company Officers serve as supervisor to their company personnel.
1.2.4.4. Company Officers are responsible for proper maintenance of the station, grounds,
CFD property, and personnel.
1.2.4.5. Company Officers are in the chain of command and shall enforce compliance with all
Cabot and CFD policies and procedures.
1.2.4.6. Company Officers will perform such other duties as the Fire Chief may direct.
1.2.5. Engineers rank next below Captain. Engineers shall rank by date of appointment and
above firefighter or as otherwise directed by the Fire Chief.

14

1.2.5.1. Engineers, under the direction of company officers, shall have full charge and
responsibility of his apparatus at all times.
1.2.5.2. Engineers shall, when authorized, act as Captain.
1.2.5.3. Engineers shall be thoroughly familiar with the tools and equipment carried and the
requirements of the basic load.
1.2.5.4. Engineers shall assure that each apparatus has the prescribed basic load of water,
hose, tools, and other equipment at all times; and, that the apparatus is restored to available
service without delay upon return from the fire ground.
1.2.5.5. Engineers will complete the daily and/or weekly apparatus checks and inventory
reports to include logging completion of checks/inventories in station computers.
1.2.5.6. Engineers will inform the company officer of any repairs or supplies required to the
apparatus. Any condition that would take the apparatus out of service shall be immediately
reported to a chief officer.
1.2.5.7. Engineers will perform such other duties as the Fire Chief may direct.
1.2.6. Firefighters rank next below Engineers. Firefighters shall rank by date of appointment
as otherwise directed by the Fire Chief.
1.2.6.1. Firefighters will respond to alarms prepared to obey and execute the orders and
instructions of the duly appointed officers of the CFD.
1.2.6.2. Firefighters are to adhere to the Policies and Procedures as set forth herein.
1.2.6.3. Firefighters are expected to respond and assist, as assigned, to certain medical
emergencies and may be exposed to blood or other bodily fluids.
1.2.6.4. Any person entering the service of the CFD shall be on a probationary period for a
period of one year. During this period, the firefighter will be given abilities tests and
examinations to determine his/her fitness and ability to perform such duties.
1.2.6.5. Firefighters will perform such other duties as the Fire Chief may direct.
1.3. Policy #3 - Training
1.3.1. In order to ensure safety, maintain proficiency, and operate efficiently, it is critical that
CFD firefighters and officers meet periodic training requirements.
1.3.2. The CFD training officer schedules and conducts department-wide, shift-wide, and
company-level training drills as directed by the Fire Chief.

15

CFD firefighters and officers are required to attend training drills. Members missing drills are
required to meet with their company officer for one-on-one training covering the topic of the
drill. Members must then meet with a chief officer to ensure all concerns are addressed.
All members are encouraged to attend classes at and through the Arkansas Fire Academy,
National Fire Academy, and other educational facilities as the CFD budget may allow. They
are encouraged to enroll in such courses and programs as to improve their knowledge,
technical skills, leadership ability, and professionalism.
1.3.3. Firefighters at any rank may be required to attend and successfully complete certain
classes.
1.3.4. Responsibility for planning and conducting in-house training sessions may be vested in
any qualified member. This member shall be appointed by the Fire Chief.
1.3.5. Training objectives are related to the levels of proficiency as required by NFPA
standards for officers and firefighters.
1.3.6. All firefighters (excluding chief officers) will train and document a minimum of two (2)
hours per shift while on duty. The training will be correspondent to a training schedule
approved by the Fire Chief.
1.3.7. While attending any training session, all firefighters will wear the appropriate CFD
uniform with required personal protective equipment. Deviations must be approved by a chief
officer.
1.3.8. CFD personnel will ensure documentation of all training is provided to the CFD training
officer who will place it in individual training files.
1.4. Policy #4 - Fire Prevention: the prevention of fires through programs, presentations,
inspections, pre-planning, and enforcement of the adopted Fire Prevention Code.
1.4.1. The Fire Chief, when qualified in accordance with Arkansas Municipal Code, shall
remain as the fire marshal until such time as the Fire Chief deems that a separate fire marshal
is necessary. The fire marshal shall be appointed by the Fire Chief on the basis of
qualifications.
1.4.2. The Fire Chief may detail members of the CFD as inspectors/origin and cause
investigators as necessary.
1.4.3. The CFD is responsible for fire and safety inspections. Any CFD member may be
trained and detailed accordingly. Inspectors will be within the CFD chain of command.
1.4.4. Inspectors/investigators will conduct themselves as representatives of the CFD in a
worthy and professional manner, being neat in appearance, in uniform, with badge visible for
identification.

16

1.5. Policy #5 – Awards and Decorations
1.5.1. Awards Committee: The awards committee is comprised of Chief Officers
1.5.2. Nomination Procedure: Any member of the Cabot Fire Department may nominate
another member for an award or commendation. Supervisors will recognize exceptional
performance by personnel under their supervision. Whenever a member of the Cabot Fire
Department has performed an act or rendered service that qualifies for recognition, the
nomination procedure will be as follows:
1.5.2.1. A written nomination will be submitted in a timely manner, in standard memorandum
format, and must include a detailed and accurate account of the circumstances surrounding the
act or incident.
1.5.2.2. The nomination will be forwarded through the chain of command to the Fire Chief
accompanied by any comments or additional facts.
1.5.2.3. After review by the Fire Chief, the nomination will be forwarded to the Awards
Committee for deliberation and recommendation as to the appropriate award such action
merits.
1.5.2.4. The Awards Committee will submit a recommendation to the Fire Chief for approval.
1.5.2.5. Upon approval by the Fire Chief, the Awards Committee will prepare the appropriate
award. Presentation of awards will be made during an awards ceremony or other special
occasion determined by the Awards Committee.
1.5.3. Written appeals regarding recommendations shall be forwarded to the Fire Chief
through the chain of command. The Fire Chief shall determine the final disposition of
appeals.
1.5.4. Subsequent Awards: An employee may earn unlimited awards conceivable provided the
firefighter becomes eligible through additional actions or service. Subsequent awards will be
designated by a silver Maltese cross displayed on the ribbon or drape of the medal for each
subsequent award up to the fifth award. A gold Maltese cross will be displayed in lieu of a
sixth award. Devices will be centered on the ribbon or drape and displayed horizontally.
1.5.5. Awards Criteria Specifications: There shall be three (3) types of awards/decorations
awarded to members of the Cabot Fire Department for exemplary duty. They are
Certificateare Certificate, Ribbon, or Medal and are defined as follows:
1.5.5.1. Medal of Valor: Awarded to a Firefighter for performance above and beyond the call
of duty at extreme personal risk having been instrumental in rescuing and saving another’s
life.

17

1.5.5.2. Medal of Gallantry: Awarded to a Firefighter who, at great personal risk, has been
instrumental in rescuing and saving another from possible death.
1.5.5.3. Medal of Courage: Awarded to a Firefighter who was involved in an act of bravery or
who shows initiative and capability.
1.5.5.4. Distinguished Service Medal: Awarded to those Firefighters who have performed acts
of heroism which are not directly fire related.
1.5.5.5. Final Alarm Medal: Presented to the family of a deceased Firefighter during a wake.
Awarded to a Firefighter who is laid out, whether in full dress uniform or not, one who is
active or life member of a fire company.
1.5.5.6. Officer of the Year Medal: Presented to the Officer of the Year. The Officer of the
Year is chosen by the Chief.
1.5.5.7. Engineer of the Year Medal: Presented to the Engineer of the Year. The Engineer of
the Year is chosen by majority vote will all officers having one Vote.
1.5.5.8. Firefighter of the Year Medal: Presented to the Firefighter of the Year. The
Firefighter of the Year is chosen by majority vote with all officers having one vote.
1.5.5.9. Service Recognition Medal: Awarded to those Firefighters in acknowledgement of
their long and faithful fire service. Rewarded at 10 years, 15 years, and 20 years respectably.
1.5.5.10. Unit Citation Ribbons: Awarded to groups of firefighters for team efforts that
resulted in quality improvement.
1.5.5.11. Campaign Ribbons: Awarded to Firefighters who were present at a large-scale
incident that is specified by the Fire Chief or Mayor as deserving of recognition.
1.5.6. Display of Awards: When wearing Dress or Class “A” uniform Firefighters will display
all decorations received in a manner prescribed within the guidelines of the Cabot Fire
Department.
1.5.7. Additional Awards / Decorations: Additional awards / decorations may be added to this
standard in the future.
1.5.8. Order of Precedence: Medal of Valor, Medal of Gallantry, Medal of Courage,
Distinguished Service Medal, Final Alarm Medal, Officer of the Year Medal, Engineer of the
Year Medal, Firefighter of the Year Medal, Service Recognition Medal, Unit Citation Ribbon,
Campaign Ribbon (most recent campaign has the highest precedence)

2. SECTION II - HIRING AND PROMOTION PROCEDURES
2.1. Application Process
2.1.1. Persons desiring employment with the CFD may complete an online application via the
city website. A computer is available at Cabot City Hall for those who do not otherwise have
access to one.
2.1.2. When the fire department schedules a new applicant test, applicants who have
completed or updated an online application within the past six months will be notified via
email addresses on the application.
2.1.3. Applicants must be at least 18 years of age by the date of the physical test. Pass
physical and written test which will be administered by or through the CFD.
2.1.4. Based on the number of open positions, finalists will be interviewed for specific
positions.
2.2. The CFD does not discriminate against anyone on the basis of race, color, sex, religion,
age, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
2.3. Full-time firefighters are required to successfully complete the minimum standards class
through the Arkansas Fire Academy (unless already certified to AFA standards) within one (1)
year of being hired. Exceptions may be made by the Fire Chief, based on class availability
and extenuating circumstances.
2.4. Full-time firefighters shall successfully complete an accredited Emergency Medical
Technician-Basic course, and pass the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians
exam and be licensed in the State of Arkansas. The applicant will have 12 months from the
start of class to successfully pass both the written and practical exams. Failure to successfully
complete the course will result in termination from the CFD.
2.5. Full-time firefighters shall be certified to a minimum level of HazMat Operations through
the State Emergency Response Commission or equivalent.
2.6. Part-time firefighters will complete AFA modules 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 17 and Arkansas
Forestry Commission Wild Land Firefighting before filling shift vacancies or participating in
firefighting operations.
2.7. Promotion Process
2.7.1. Engineer: Personal qualifications for personnel who wish to promote to the position of
Engineer will include the following:
2.7.1.1. Possess a valid Arkansas driver’s license

19

2.7.1.2. Be certified as a Firefighter II as recognized by International Fire Service
Accreditation Congress (IFSAC) or Pro-Board.
2.7.1.3. Possess current license/certification as an Emergency Medical Technician as
recognized by the Arkansas Department of Health and Human Services
2.7.1.4. Have completed two years of continuous full-time service as a firefighter within the
Cabot Fire Department
2.7.1.5. Successfully completed IFSAC/Pro-board Driver/Operator course.
2.7.1.6. Received a “Fully Satisfactory”5.0 or higher on most recent performance evaluation.
2.7.1.7. Pass written promotional exam with a minimum score of 70%.
2.7.1.8. Pass practical application test.
Currently meet the minimum requirements of department physical fitness standards.
2.7.2. Company Officer: Personal qualifications for personnel who wish to promote to the
position of Company Officer will include the following:
2.7.2.1. Possess a valid Arkansas driver’s license
2.7.2.2. Be certified as a Firefighter II as recognized by International Fire Service
Accreditation Congress (IFSAC) or Pro-Board.
2.7.2.3. Possess current license/certification as an Emergency Medical Technician as
recognized by the Arkansas Department of Health and Human Services
